title.narrative: Strengthening Public Financial Management Program, Subprogram 2

description.narrative: The proposed program is part of the long-standing support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to strengthen governance and institutional capacity in Cambodia through public financial management (PFM). It assists reforms to bolster (i) the policy and regulatory framework for expenditure and revenue management, (ii) the implementation capacity of line ministries, and (iii) external audit functions. Subprogram 2 contributes to the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): (i) promoting gender equality and empowering all women and girls at all levels (SDG 5.c); (ii) integrating climate change measures into national policies, strategies, and planning (SDG 13.2); and (iii) developing effective, accountable, and transparent institutions at all levels (SDG 16.6). The program is aligned with pillar IV (improve governance) of ADB's country partnership strategy (CPS), 2019-2023, for Cambodia.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1. The National Assembly adopted the Public Finance System Law, and the government implemented the Budget System Reform Strategy (BSRS) 2018−2025 to (i) modernize public financial management (PFM) systems, (ii) improve budget-policy linkages, (iii) align resources with country priorities, (iv) improve expenditure management, and (v) institutionalize reforms under the consolidated action plan for stage 3 of the Public Financial Management Reform Program (PFMRP) (CAP-3) (General Department of Budget (GDB) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) for drafting the law and BSRS; various general departments of the MEF; and General Secretariat of PFM Reform for CAP 3). 2.2. The government operationalized its medium-term fiscal framework and the medium-term budget framework to deliver (i) improved revenue and expenditure forecasting for 2021-2023; (ii) defined budget ceilings by line ministries; and (iii) risk assessment to improve macroeconomic stability and public debt management. (GDB of MEF). 2.3. The government implemented the annual budget circular, commencing in 2016, to integrate gender equality considerations into the budget strategic plans of line ministries and public institutions (GDB of MEF). 2.4. The government implemented (i) medium-term resource mobilization strategy (MTRMS) 2014-2018, which achieved an increase of revenue by 0.5 per centage point of GDP per year; (ii) MTRMS 2019−2023; and (iii) the National Assembly adopted the Law on Non-Tax Revenue to strengthen non-tax revenue administration (General Department of Taxation of MEF). 2.5. The government implemented the Public Investment Management Reform Strategy (PIMRS) 2019-2025 to improve planning and expenditure management and align externally financed projects and programs with public investment priorities. (GDB of MEF). 2.6. The government operationalized the FMIS at the National Treasury to generate timely and accurate International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)-compliant financial reports for the preparation of cash basis financial statements to achieve greater operational efficiency, timely budget information, and improved budget transparency. (Department of Information and Communication; and General Department of National Treasury of MEF). 2.7. The government adopted the internal audit manual in line with international internal auditing standards, included principles and guidelines for internal control of ICT and performance audits and implemented with immediate effect to improve reliability and boost performance accountability. (General Department of Internal Audit of MEF). 2.8. The government implemented the Public Debt Management Strategy 2019-2023 to: (i) define ceilings for government guarantees, including guarantees for the PPPs and SOPs; (ii) allocate an additional 5% of the total annual amount of public debt services for contingent liabilities; and (iii) improve debt reporting and transparency by regular publishing of the public debt statistical bulletin to ensure sustainable debt management practices (General Department of International Cooperation and Debt Management of MEF).

2. The government (i) implemented the BSP and annual program budgeting to better integrate capital and current budgets, incorporate poverty, gender equality, and climate change adaptation; and (ii) submitted the annual financial and performance reports commencing in 2022h to MEF by six-line ministries (MEF and line ministries). 2.10. The government (i) rolled out FMIS implementation to line ministries including the implementation of business processes and change management strategies implemented by six-line ministries; and (ii) commenced ICT and performance audits to improve efficiency, boost the reliability of ICT systems, and improve performance accountability. (MEF and line ministries).

3. The National Audit Authority (NAA) implemented (i) regulations to support the Audit Law; and (ii) guidelines on financial, compliance, and performance audits which are aligned with international auditing standards to strengthen its oversight responsibility (NAA). 2.12. The NAA (i) implemented the strategic development plan 2017-2021 to strengthen oversight responsibility for public expenditure management; and (ii) summited annually with the National Assembly and published publicly the audited public financial statements, in accordance with the law on audit, to improve transparency and accountability of public expenditures. (NAA).
